main_text.l: Lacedæmon in communionem reipu-blicæ Achaicæ recepta.

SEd vicit sententia Lycortæ, & Lacedæmon in communionem societatis Achaicæ est recepta, atque hoc decretum columnæ, quod fieri in iis, quæ firma & immota censebantur, solebat, inscriptum: & ex exulum numero illi, qui nunquàm ingrati atque improbi in Achæos animi signum edidissent. Manstitque ab eo tempore Lacedæmon confors reipublicæ Achaicæ. His rebus confectis, missus Romam est ab Achæis Bippus Argivus, à Lacedæmoniis Charon, qui de omnibus senatum facerent certiorem. Ab exulibus autem Cletis quoque istuc legatus, qui ipsorum causam contra legatos cæteros tueretur. Qui cum omnes Romæ abunde auditi essent, senatus quidem nihil eorum, quæ à civitate Spartanâ acta erant, reprehendit, aut indignè se ferre ostendit: exulibus verò promisit, ad Achæos se scripturum de illis in patriam restituendis. page.notes: The text is clear, apart from the marked words. "missus" at the start of the line after "His rebus confectis," is hard to read at the scan edge; "Messenen" and "missus" are doubtful, so I marked them [?] or left the first letters as read. The right margin has many small fragments (letters, reference marks such as "m", "ut", "e") that I could not read reliably. They are shown only as illegible placeholders above. Several marks are printed directly beside lines 'restituendis', 'Bippo', 'Messenen' and 'omn-', but I could not read the text. The word "omn-" at the line end is followed by "hun" in the lower right, which is the catchword. Its exact form is doubtful. A faint mark at the bottom left ("JOL" or similar) is likely a gathering sign or show-through; it is left out. The line-end "restituen dis" appears joined without a printed hyphen; I have written it as "restituendis" in the note description only.
